notes:
I don't have any notes for you this time, because the research didn't get done. My first try at fetching the commentary pages failed due to a bug in my code. When I tried to fix it, the tool told me I had no more fetch attempts left for this turn. I never read a single page: not Enduring Word, Precept Austin, BibleHub (Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit, Wesley), NET Bible, New Advent or any of the other sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for every point. Notes written from my own memory would break that rule, so I haven't written any.

If you send the request again in a new message, I'll start with these pages, which cover all three parts of your brief:

- **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/micah-5/, preceptaustin.org/micah-5-commentary, and the Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit and Barnes commentaries on Micah 5 at biblehub.com.
- **Protestant differences:** wesley.nnu.edu (Wesley's Notes) for the Methodist view; ligonier.org, thegospelcoalition.org and monergism.com (Calvin) for the Reformed view; desiringgod.org, spurgeon.org and gty.org for the Baptist view; lcms.org and 1517.org for the Lutheran view; enduringword.com and ag.org for the Pentecostal view. On verse 2 these are likely to agree, so I'll only report a split where the pages actually show one. Verses 3 and 5–8 (who "the remnant" and "the seven shepherds" are) seem the likeliest places to find one.
- **Other views:** the netbible.org notes and bibleodyssey.org for modern scholarship, especially on verse 2 ("from the days of eternity") and verse 3 ("she who is in labor"). For the Catholic and Orthodox readings: newadvent.org (Church Fathers and the Catholic Encyclopedia), catholic.com and oca.org. These matter most for verses 2–3, where Mary and Christ's eternal origin come up.
